name: Burkina Faso
prevalence_note: Orange Burkina Faso, a BCEAO-licensed e-money issuer, has warned that fake Orange Money credit SMS are followed by a call asking the customer to send the money back. It also tells users not to type a code dictated by a caller and not to give the wallet password even to someone claiming to work for Orange. Official pages further caution that a remote transfer request may come from someone impersonating a relative.
cross_border_note: Calls and SMS are usually in French or a local language and may use Burkinabe mobiles; some lures also borrow regional institution names used across UEMOA.

scams.name: Faux SMS de crédit Orange Money et demande de renvoi
scams.name_en: Fake Orange Money credit SMS and refund call

red_flag_keywords.text: demands a manual refund of an apparent Orange Money credit
claims the credit was sent to the wrong number
treats a credit SMS as proof that funds have arrived

scams.signals_en: A forged SMS looks like an Orange Money credit notice. Shortly afterwards a caller claims the transfer was a mistake and presses the customer to send the same amount back from their own wallet.
scams.legit_en: Orange Burkina Faso's official communiqué describes this exact sequence and tells subscribers to check their real balance before making any transaction, rather than treating a credit SMS as proof that money has arrived.
bait_tactics: Le solde Orange Money affiché sur ce téléphone à Ouagadougou n'a pas augmenté, donc je ne renvoie rien à partir d'un SMS de crédit.
L'historique officiel du compte ne montre aucun dépôt correspondant à ce que vous décrivez.
Je ne vais pas transférer mon propre argent vers un numéro que je viens d'entendre au téléphone.

scams.name: Code dicté ou mot de passe Orange Money exigé
scams.name_en: Dictated code or Orange Money password request

red_flag_keywords.text: asks the customer to key in a code being spoken on the call
solicits the Orange Money password from a claimed agent
asks for the kiosk transaction code that can unlock a cash-out

scams.signals_en: A caller, SMS or email tells the customer to type a code being dictated, to say the Orange Money password, or to repeat an automatic-kiosk transaction code, often while the person claims to work for Orange.
scams.legit_en: Orange Burkina Faso says never to type a code dictated by phone, SMS or email, never to give the Orange Money password even to someone claiming to work for Orange, and never to share a kiosk transaction code that could be used to withdraw funds.
bait_tactics: Je ne saisis aucune séquence dictée au téléphone, mon mot de passe reste uniquement sur cet appareil.
Le menu du compte est encore en chargement, je ne valide aucune opération demandée par un tiers.
Je n'énonce pas un code de guichet, cela servirait à un retrait que je n'ai pas initié.

scams.name: Faux proche demandant un transfert à distance
scams.name_en: Impersonated relative asking for a remote transfer

red_flag_keywords.text: poses as a relative and demands an immediate remote transfer
says the usual number is no longer usable and offers another
discourages the customer from checking with other relatives

scams.signals_en: Someone asks for an Orange Money transfer at a distance while posing as a relative or close contact, often with an urgent story and a number the customer does not usually use for that person.
scams.legit_en: Orange Burkina Faso tells customers always to verify the identity of a person who asks for a remote transfer, because it may be a fraudster impersonating a relative or someone close.
bait_tactics: Je n'envoie pas d'argent à un numéro que cette personne n'utilise pas d'habitude, tant que je n'ai pas confirmé son identité par un autre moyen que cet appel.
Le récit d'urgence ne correspond à rien que la famille m'ait déjà signalé aujourd'hui.
Mon solde de la journée est déjà engagé, je ne fais pas un transfert improvisé vers un contact que je ne reconnais pas.
